newsitem.title: USA: Central Maine Power to sell generating assets.
newsitem.headline: Central Maine Power to sell generating assets.

text.p: Central Maine Power Co said Monday it would ask regulators for permission to sell its electricity-generating assets.

The utility said it is taking the step in advance of the expected market deregulation in Maine, and hopes putting the assets on the market now will allow it to take advantage of better market conditions.
A deregulation proposal drafted by the state Public Utilities Commission would have utilities divest generating assets by the year 2000.
The Maine legislature is considering several deregulation bills, but it is unclear if lawmakers will enact any changes this year.

"We believe a sale sooner rather than later may offer the best opportunity for customers to benefit by lowering the amount of stranded costs that would need to be recovered through electricity rates," Central Maine Power President David Flanagan said in a prepared statement.
The company said buyer interest in a similar sale proposed by the New England Electric System "suggests that a favorable market environment may exist today for the sale of generation assets."
While the generating assets would be put on the market "in the next several weeks," any "actual sale will take considerably longer and is subject to regulatory approvals," it said.
Central Maine Power said cash proceeds from the sale would be used to reduce its debts. Lower debt obligations would likely allow the utlity to reduce its rate, it said.
